title: What is the difference between CrudRepository, PagingAndSortingRepository, and JpaRepository in Spring Data?
keyPoints: CrudRepository provides basic CRUD: save, findById, findAll (Iterable), delete, count, and existsById.
PagingAndSortingRepository extends CrudRepository with findAll(Pageable) and findAll(Sort) for pagination and sorting.
JpaRepository extends PagingAndSortingRepository and adds JPA-specific operations: saveAll, flush, saveAndFlush, deleteAllInBatch, and getReferenceById.
JpaRepository overrides findAll to return a List instead of an Iterable, which is more convenient.
deleteAllInBatch issues a single bulk JPQL DELETE that bypasses cascades and lifecycle callbacks.
Expose the narrowest interface that meets the need to communicate intent clearly.

s1_definition.oneliner: CrudRepository is basic CRUD, PagingAndSortingRepository adds paging and sorting, and JpaRepository adds JPA batch and flush power.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **CrudRepository** – provides basic create, read, update, and delete operations: save, findById, findAll (returns Iterable), delete, count, and existsById.
- **PagingAndSortingRepository** – extends CrudRepository with findAll(Pageable) returning a Page and findAll(Sort) returning sorted results.
- **JpaRepository** – extends PagingAndSortingRepository and adds JPA-specific batch and flush operations: saveAll, flush, saveAndFlush, deleteAllInBatch, getReferenceById, and overrides findAll to return a List.
- **Inheritance chain** – CrudRepository < PagingAndSortingRepository < JpaRepository, each level adding more capability.
- **Interface segregation** – expose the narrowest interface that meets the need, so the contract communicates intent.
s1_definition.analogy: Think of three tiers of bank-teller training at National Bank of India. CrudRepository is the basic teller who can open, read, update, and close accounts one at a time. PagingAndSortingRepository is a teller who can also hand you results twenty at a time, sorted by date. JpaRepository is the senior teller who can additionally do bulk operations efficiently: save a whole stack at once, flush immediately to the vault, or batch-delete, which is exactly what National Bank of India needs for heavy batch processing.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Repository Inheritance Chain
  ============================================

  +-----------------------+
  |   CrudRepository      |  <- Spring Data Commons
  |-----------------------|
  | save()                |
  | findById()            |
  | findAll() -> Iterable |
  | delete()              |
  | count()               |
  | existsById()          |
  +----------+------------+
             |
             v
  +-----------------------------+
  | PagingAndSortingRepository  |  <- Spring Data Commons
  |-----------------------------|
  | findAll(Pageable) -> Page   |
  | findAll(Sort) -> Iterable   |
  +----------+------------------+
             |
             v
  +-----------------------------+
  |      JpaRepository          |  <- Spring Data JPA
  |-----------------------------|
  | saveAll()                   |
  | flush()                     |
  | saveAndFlush()              |
  | deleteAllInBatch()          |
  | getReferenceById()          |
  | findAll() -> List (override)|
  +-----------------------------+
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
These three interfaces form an inheritance chain of increasing capability at National Bank of India. CrudRepository provides the essentials: save, findById returning an Optional, findAll returning an Iterable, delete, count, and existsById. PagingAndSortingRepository extends it and adds findAll with a Pageable and findAll with a Sort, which is where Rajesh gets the page-size-sort abstraction for listing thousands of accounts. JpaRepository extends that further and layers on JPA-specific power: saveAll for bulk persistence, flush and saveAndFlush for explicit flush control, deleteAllInBatch for a single bulk delete, and it overrides findAll to return a List.

The guiding principle Pankaj enforces is interface segregation: expose the narrowest interface that meets the need. A simple customer-lookup service extends CrudRepository so a reviewer immediately knows it does only basic operations. A paginated statement screen extends PagingAndSortingRepository. A nightly batch job that imports a hundred thousand accounts extends JpaRepository because it needs saveAll, flush, and deleteAllInBatch.

The senior cautions are that deleteAllInBatch issues a bulk JPQL DELETE that bypasses cascades and @PreRemove callbacks, that saveAndFlush is frequently misused inside loops in a way that destroys batching, and that getReferenceById throws its not-found exception lazily so when you need to confirm existence you should use findById instead.

Remember one sentence: CrudRepository gives basic CRUD, PagingAndSortingRepository adds pagination, and JpaRepository adds batch, flush, and List returns for JPA-specific power.
